Happy to help with that. What's the order number, and either the name it ships to or the postcode?

Used the store-orders skill

Thanks John, I've got it. Order Shop····, the Hammer Miner DC08, shipped and was delivered on September 29, so there's nothing left to cancel on it.

What's going on with it? If it arrived faulty I can start an RMA, and if it's something else tell me and I'll see what we can do.
2 pools I connected to for over 24hrs says the hashrate is one tenth of the devices 440+ hashrate

Most likely it's the pool, not the unit. Pool-side hashrate is averaged from accepted shares, so if the share difficulty is set too high for a 480 MH/s miner it reads a fraction of the real rate until it settles, sometimes days.

What does the miner's own dashboard show? If it reports 440+ locally, the hardware is fine and we fix it in the pool settings.

Quickest hands-on help is our Discord, mention JD (@nullhashrate): https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

I've tried that and the f2pool doesn not have that option.  litecoinpool setting the d=X parameter does nothing either.  Research and such indicates either a firmware issue or a voltage issue on the internal chips that logs do not show
Handed to the team · hashrate fault beyond product facts, needs JD

That's past what I can call from here, so I've put it in front of JD, who handles the hardware and firmware side. Stay in this chat and he'll jump in, and if you step away the answer comes to your email.

One thing he'll ask: has the unit been overclocked or had its firmware modified at all? Your order also carries the Harlo OS Diagnostics and 3-month RMA, so if it is a chip or voltage fault you're covered.
Nope straight out of the box and running in normal mode

Good, that keeps you fully covered. Stock firmware, normal mode, a tenth of rated hashrate on two pools, that's a unit fault until proven otherwise, and JD has it.

If he lands on a hardware fault, it goes through RMA and you get a return label: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12t6skK21Qb8GfAdUQ9nOhJ1tVINJ60T3AIAsyhBwnYM/viewform

Don't fill it in yet, let JD look first so you're not shipping a unit that a firmware reflash fixes.

FYI this log message means that the Hardware errored 33 times and the BD is a failure in voltage [2026-10-02 14:47:41] I (625392) SYS_MON: Hashrate: 441.21 MH/s | shares: 88 | rej shares: 0 | hw: 33 | BD: 13023 | PoolDiff: 8192

Thanks, that line actually helps. It reads 441.21 MH/s locally with 88 accepted and zero rejected, so the chips are producing their rated work. PoolDiff 8192 is high for a 480 MH/s unit, which is exactly how the pool side averages out low.

I won't call what BD and hw mean on this board myself, JD will, and he has your log now. He's picking the chat up from here.
I am getting roughly 40 hardware errors per 7 minutes.  This is an issue and I think this unit is broken.

Fair enough, and I'm not going to talk you out of it. Forty hardware errors in seven minutes on a stock unit in normal mode is worth a hardware look.

Go ahead and file the RMA now, your order carries the Diagnostics and 3-month RMA cover: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12t6skK21Qb8GfAdUQ9nOhJ1tVINJ60T3AIAsyhBwnYM/viewform

You'll get a return label back. Processing runs up to 10 days once it reaches the warehouse. JD still has your log, so if it turns out to be firmware he'll say so first.
